recognize_zh: 低倍下可見許多母細胞成群聚集成小團塊（clumps），散在紅血球之間，另有不少破碎的淡紫色塗抹細胞；巨核母細胞容易彼此黏聚成團，這是 ML-DS／急性巨核母細胞白血病在塗片上常見的低倍線索。
features: Low-power smear with numerous small cohesive clusters of blasts scattered among red cells
Blasts are small to medium with dark round nuclei and scant cytoplasm; fine detail not resolvable at this magnification
Cytoplasmic blebs and platelet budding cannot be assessed at this power
describe_en: Low-power view of a smear, most consistent with peripheral blood or a hemodiluted aspirate, shows numerous nucleated cells that aggregate into small cohesive clusters distributed among red cells, with frequent smudged cells in the background. At this magnification the clustered cells appear to be blasts with dark round nuclei and scant cytoplasm, but cytoplasmic blebs, granules and nucleoli cannot be evaluated. Clumping of blasts is a recognized feature of megakaryoblasts; in a patient with Down syndrome, the findings are suggestive of myeloid leukemia associated with Down syndrome, pending high-power review and flow cytometry for CD41/CD61.

ddx.dx: Metastatic small round blue cell tumor (e.g., neuroblastoma)
ddx.vs: Tumor cell clusters in children can mimic clumped megakaryoblasts, and the distinction requires CD41/CD61 expression versus CD45-negative, neural marker-positive tumor cells.
Morphologically identical, separated by neonatal onset and spontaneous regression in TAM.
Lymphoblasts usually lie as dispersed single cells rather than cohesive clumps and lack megakaryocytic markers.
